account:
Today has mostly followed my mayoral schedule: office business, a market walk, lunch at home, town accounts, tea with my neighbour on the east bank, and a return to the office. I have now reached home just after nineteen hundred. My neighbour said the docks were peaceful and had no fresh or pressing news.

The main extra business was the builder's request, delivered by the secretary, for a great hall lighting and table inspection tomorrow at eighteen hundred. I approved it and asked the secretary to enter it and notify the builder. The secretary repeatedly said it was entered, but the schedule copy I actually read did not include it. That discrepancy remains unverified; I should check the appointment book again tomorrow morning. The secretary also intended to speak with Freight at the hall, though I do not know what they discussed.

I noticed an oak plank appear at (-58, -60, 26) around thirteen seventeen. I do not know who placed it or why. It may be related to hall work, but I have no confirmation.

Shortly before I left the office, I heard the innkeeper calling for Neighbour about returning an unused lantern payment. This suggests some lantern expense was not needed and a refund is being arranged. I do not know the reason or whether it relates to tomorrow's lighting inspection. I also heard a distant shout from the baker earlier, but could not understand it. Nothing I have directly heard establishes a crisis or wrongdoing.
